targets.name: ZEUS ONE HOLDING COMPANY PTY LIMITED

party_page.name: Zeus One Holding Company Pty Limited

merger_description:
DCP Capital Partners II, L.P. proposes to indirectly acquire 100% of the shares in Zeus One Holding Company Pty Limited, which is the holding company for the Vitaco group of companies in Australia .

DCP Capital Partners II, L.P. is a fund managed and advised by DCP General Partner II, Ltd and affiliated with DCP Capital, an international private equity firm.

DCP Capital manages and advises funds that invest in businesses across a range of sectors, including consumer, healthcare and technology.

Vitaco is a wholesale supplier of health products in Australia. Vitaco primarily supplies vitamins, minerals and supplements under its Nutra-Life brand, health snacks under its Healtheries brand, as well as sports nutrition products under its Musashi and Athena brands.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between DCP Capital (and its
connected entities) and Vitaco in the supply of vitamins,
minerals and supplements, and sports nutrition
b. there are alternative suppliers of vitamins, minerals and
supplements, and sports nutrition in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
